title: Dell PowerEdge R730 vs R730xd: Every Bay, Slot and GPU Limit
excerpt: What the R730 and R730xd share, every drive bay, PCIe slot and GPU difference from Dell's documents, and which one to buy for a ZFS box or a GPU host.
gap_note: Editor decision on October 5, 2026: AI-generated marketplace pages (AliExpress wiki-ssr, Accio plp) and auto-titled benchmark comparisons (Geekbench) are treated like forum threads and do not close the gap. The AliExpress page's drive counts contradict Dell's technical guide.

claims.claim: Both servers use Intel's C610 chipset.
claims.quote: The PowerEdge R730 and R730xd servers use the Intel C610 chipset.

claims.claim: The R730 is a two-socket 2U rack server.
claims.quote: A highly versatile, two-socket 2U rack server

claims.claim: The R730xd is a 2U server that takes Xeon E5-2600 v3 or v4 processors.
claims.quote: The Dell PowerEdge R730xd systems are 2U rack servers that support up to two Intel Xeon E5-2600 v3 or Xeon E5-2600 v4

claims.claim: The technical guide covers only v3 processors, with up to 18 cores per processor.
claims.quote: The R730 and R730xd support up to two processors with up to 18 cores per processor.

claims.claim: The R730 spec sheet lists E5-2600 v4 processors with up to 22 cores.
claims.quote: Latest Intel Xeon processor E5-2600 v4 product family with up to 22 cores

claims.claim: The E5-2699 v4 has 22 cores.
claims.quote: Total Cores 22

claims.claim: The E5-2699 v4 is a 145 W part.
claims.quote: TDP 145 W

claims.claim: Dell added E5-2600 v4 support to the R630/R730/R730xd in BIOS 2.0.1.
claims.quote: Added support for Intel Xeon processor E5-2600 V4 product family.

claims.claim: BIOS 2.0.1 was released March 17, 2016.
ServeTheHome describes a BIOS upgrade path for running the E5-2699 v4 on existing platforms.
claims.quote: With a simple BIOS upgrade, it is ready to support the Broadwell-EP chips.

claims.claim: The 160 W E5-2687W v3 is in Dell's supported processor list but marked as not supported on the R730xd (so it is supported on the R730).
claims.quote: E5-2687W v3* 3.1GHz 25M 9.6GT/s 1866 10/20 Turbo 160W ... *Not supported on the R730xd

claims.claim: The R730xd owner's manual caps the 2.5-inch chassis at 145 W processors (note in the standard operating temperature table).
claims.quote: The 2.5-inch hard drive chassis supports a maximum of 145 W processors.

claims.claim: The 120 W limit for the 3.5-inch chassis is listed under Dell's expanded operating temperature restrictions.
claims.quote: Expanded operating temperature restrictions ... The 3.5-inch hard drive chassis supports a maximum of 120 W processor.

claims.claim: The standard operating temperature range is 10 to 35C.
claims.quote: Continuous operation (for altitude less than 950 m or 3117 ft) 10°C to 35°C (50°F to 95°F)

claims.claim: The 22-core E5-2699 v4 is a 145 W part (corroborating source).
claims.quote: 22 cores and 44 threads ... 145w TDP

claims.claim: Both have 24 DIMM slots, 12 per processor.
claims.quote: The system supports up to 12 DIMMs per processor (up to 24 DIMMs in a dual-processor configuration).

claims.claim: RDIMMs and LRDIMMs cannot be mixed in one system.
claims.quote: Only one type of DIMM is allowed per system, either RDIMM or LRDIMM.

claims.claim: The technical guide gives 768GB maximum memory and speeds up to 2133MT/s (the v3 ceiling).
claims.quote: The R730 and R730xd support up to 768GB of memory (24 DIMMs) and speeds up to 2133MT/s (2 DIMMs per channel)

claims.claim: The R730xd manual lists memory speeds up to 2400MT/s.
claims.quote: Supported memory bus frequencies are 1333MT/s, 1600 MT/s, 1866 MT/s, 2133MT/s, or 2400 MT/s.

claims.claim: DDR4-2400 support comes with the v4 processors (E5-2699 v4 memory types).
The R730 spec sheet gives up to 3TB with 128GB modules at up to 2400MT/s.
claims.quote: Up to 3TB (24 DIMM slots): 4GB/8GB/16GB/32GB/64GB/128GB DDR4 up to 2400MT/s

claims.claim: The R730xd manual gives 3,072GB for LRDIMMs and 768GB for RDIMMs with two processors.
claims.quote: LRDIMM up to 3,072 GB with dual processors ... RDIMM up to 768 GB with a dual processor

claims.claim: The technical guide was written when 64GB modules were still coming.
claims.quote: 64GB DIMMs will be available immediately post-RTS and will expand the memory footprint to 1.5TB.

claims.claim: iDRAC8 with Lifecycle Controller: Express by default, Enterprise as an upgrade.
claims.quote: iDRAC8 with Lifecycle Controller, iDRAC8 Express (default), iDRAC8 Enterprise (upgrade)

claims.claim: Both take up to two hot-plug power supplies.
claims.quote: Power supply units Up to two back-accessible, hot-plug power supplies

claims.claim: Shared PSU menu for both: 750 W Titanium AC; 495 W, 750 W or 1100 W Platinum AC; 1100 W DC (the 2s are footnote markers).
claims.quote: 750W AC (Titanium2); 495W, 750W or 1100W AC (Platinum2); 1100W DC

claims.claim: The H730P has 2GB and the H730 1GB of non-volatile cache.
claims.quote: 2GB 1866MT/s DDR3 SDRAM non-volatile cache ... 1GB 1866MT/s DDR3 SDRAM non-volatile cache

claims.claim: The base PERC is a mini card that does not use a PCIe slot.
claims.quote: The base RAID controller in the R730 and R730xd is the miniPERC, which provides a base RAID hardware controller without consuming a PCIe slot

claims.claim: PERC S130 software RAID is R730 only.
claims.quote: PERC S130 (software RAID; R730 only)

claims.claim: The S130 is available only on the 8-drive 2.5-inch configuration.
claims.quote: Only available on the 8-drive 2.5” configuration

claims.claim: Dell says the backplane option is fixed at purchase.
claims.quote: Note that the backplane option must be selected at point of purchase and cannot be changed or upgraded later.

claims.claim: Dell says a chassis cannot be reconfigured after purchase.
claims.quote: Note: A chassis cannot be reconfigured or upgraded after point of purchase.

claims.claim: R730 eight-drive systems take 3.5-inch or 2.5-inch drives.
claims.quote: up to eight 3.5-inch or 2.5-inch, internal, hot-swappable SAS, SATA, or Nearline SAS hard drives

claims.claim: R730 sixteen-drive systems are 2.5-inch (its maximum of 16 drives).
claims.quote: up to sixteen 2.5-inch, internal, hot-swappable SAS, SATA, SAS/SATA SSD, or Nearline SAS hard drives

claims.claim: R730xd: 12 x 3.5-inch plus two optional rear 2.5-inch bays.
claims.quote: Up to twelve 3.5-inch hard drives and two optional 2.5-inch back-accessible hard drives.

claims.claim: R730xd: 12 x 3.5-inch, two rear 2.5-inch and four 3.5-inch in the middle tray.
claims.quote: Up to twelve 3.5-inch hard drives, two optional 2.5-inch back-accessible hard drives and four 3.5-inch hard drives in the middle hard drive tray.

claims.claim: R730xd: 24 x 2.5-inch plus two rear.
claims.quote: Up to twenty-four 2.5-inch hard drives and two optional 2.5-inch back-accessible hard drives

claims.claim: R730xd NVMe: up to four U.2 drives in slots 20 to 23 of the 24-bay front.
claims.quote: Up to twenty 2.5-inch hard drives, up to four 2.5-inch (U.2) NVMe drives (in slots 20 to 23) and up to two optional back-accessible hard drives.

claims.claim: R730xd hybrid: 18 x 1.8-inch plus 8 x 3.5-inch plus two rear.
claims.quote: Up to eighteen 1.8-inch hard drives, up to eight 3.5-inch hard drives, and up to two 2.5-inch back-accessible hard drives.

claims.claim: The R730xd tops out at 28 drives.
claims.quote: Twenty eight hard drive systems

claims.claim: The 1.8-inch drives are SATA SSDs, 18 of them alongside eight 3.5-inch drives.
claims.quote: 18 x 1.8” SATA SSDs + 8 x 3.5” SATA, NL-SAS HDDs

claims.claim: The middle tray sits behind the fan assembly and holds four 3.5-inch drives.
claims.quote: The hard drive tray is located behind the cooling fan assembly. It supports four 3.5 inch hard drives.

claims.claim: The middle tray works only in certain 12-bay configurations.
claims.quote: The hard drive tray is supported only on certain configurations of the 3.5 inch (x12) systems.

claims.claim: Middle-tray systems need low-profile heat sinks and no cooling shroud.
claims.quote: Systems that support the internal hard drive tray require low-profile heat sinks and do not require or support a cooling shroud.

claims.claim: The rear pair and the middle tray are backplane options.
claims.quote: 3.5 inch (x12) SAS/SATA backplane, 3.5 inch (x4) SAS/SATA backplane on the hard drive tray and 2.5 inch (x2) SAS/SATA backplane (back)

claims.claim: The R730 does not support Express Flash (NVMe) drives; the R730xd supports up to four in the 2.5-inch chassis.
claims.quote: The PowerEdge R730xd has an option to support up to four hot-plug Express Flash PCIe SSDs in the 2.5” chassis. The R730 does not support Express Flash drives.

claims.claim: StorageReview confirms four PCIe SSD bays on the R730xd.
claims.quote: 4x PCIe SSD with common slot backplane technology

claims.claim: InfoWorld confirms up to four NVMe SSDs on the R730xd.
claims.quote: You can also include up to four Express Flash NVMe PCIe SSDs to satisfy the highest I/O demands.

claims.claim: The R730 has seven PCIe slots and the R730xd six.
claims.quote: The R730 supports up to 7 PCIe expansion cards; R730xd supports up to 6 PCIe expansion cards

claims.claim: Both add a dedicated PERC slot to their PCIe 3.0 slots.
claims.quote: R730: Up to 7 PCIe 3.0 slots plus dedicated PERC slot R730xd: Up to 6 PCIe 3.0 slots plus dedicated PERC slot

claims.claim: Riser 1 has three low-profile x8 slots; riser 2 has a full-height x16 and a full-height x8.
claims.quote: Riser 1 Slot 1 half-height low-profile x8 ... Riser 2 Slot 4 full-height full-length x16 Riser 2 Slot 5 full-height full-length x8

claims.claim: R730 riser 3: two full-height x8 slots (6 and 7), or one x16 with the alternative riser.
claims.quote: Left riser 3 7 Full height CPU1 PCIe 3.0 x8 (x16 connector) 75W ... Left riser 3 alternative 6 Full height CPU1 PCIe 3.0 x16 (x16 connector) 75W

claims.claim: R730xd riser 3 offers only the single x16 slot 6.
claims.quote: 6 3 (alternate) Processor 1 Full Height Full Length x16 x16

claims.claim: Slots 1 through 4 need both processors (R730xd manual; the R730 manual has the same note).
claims.quote: When using slots 1 through 4 on the riser, ensure that both the processors are installed on the system.

claims.claim: A one-processor R730 keeps slots 5 to 7, which connect to processor 1.
claims.quote: Center riser 2 5 Full height CPU1 ... Left riser 3 6 Full height CPU1 ... Left riser 3 7 Full height CPU1

claims.claim: A one-processor R730xd keeps slots 5 and 6, which connect to processor 1.
claims.quote: 5 2 Processor 1 Full Height Full Length x 8 x16 6 3 (alternate) Processor 1 Full Height Full Length x16 x16

claims.claim: The R730 takes an optional slimline SATA DVD-ROM or DVD+/-RW drive; the R730xd takes no optical drive.
claims.quote: The R730 supports one optional slimline SATA DVD-ROM drive or DVD+/-RW drive; R730xd does not support an internal optical drive

claims.claim: R730 owner's manual confirms the optional optical drive.
claims.quote: The system supports one optional SATA DVD-ROM drive or DVD+/-RW drive.

claims.claim: R730 has an LCD control panel; R730xd has an LED panel.
claims.quote: LCD control panel Provides user access to buttons, display, and I/O interfaces (R730 only) LED panel Indicates the status of system conditions (R730xd only)

claims.claim: R730 has two front USB ports; R730xd has one.
claims.quote: USB connectors R730: 2 front, 2 back, and 1 internal R730xd: 1 front, 2 back, and 1 internal

claims.claim: The R730xd's front USB port is the iDRAC Direct management port.
claims.quote: USB management port/iDRAC Direct

claims.claim: The R730's vFlash slot is at the front; the R730xd's is at the back.
claims.quote: the R730 slot is located in the front of the system and the R730x slot is located in the back

claims.claim: InfoWorld's R730xd used its rear pair as a RAID-1 operating system mirror.
claims.quote: Two more 2.5-inch drives on the rear provide a RAID-1 mirror for the operating system disk.

claims.claim: Dell's 1.8-inch SSD options topped out at 960GB.
claims.quote: SATA SSD (read intensive, 6Gb) N/A 480GB, 960GB

claims.claim: Dell ranks the 1.8-inch hybrid as the loudest R730xd chassis at idle.
claims.quote: from the quietest to the loudest: ... 24 x 2.5” chassis ... 12 x 3.5” chassis ... 8 x 3.5” + 18 x 1.8” SSD chassis

claims.claim: OpenZFS says hardware RAID controllers should not be used with ZFS.
claims.quote: Hardware RAID controllers should not be used with ZFS.

claims.claim: OpenZFS recommends an HBA.
claims.quote: It is best to use a HBA instead of a RAID controller, for both performance and reliability.

claims.claim: OpenZFS: hardware RAID limits ZFS self-healing.
claims.quote: Hardware RAID will limit opportunities for ZFS to perform self healing on checksum failures.

claims.claim: The HBA330 is an 8-port LSI 3008 card.
claims.quote: Dell Adapter SAS I/O controller, 8-port with LSI 3008 chipset

claims.claim: The HBA330 runs in non-RAID pass-through mode.
claims.quote: Non-RAID or pass through mode: Yes

claims.claim: Dell's HBA330 Mini firmware page lists the R730 and R730xd as compatible (component type SAS Non-RAID).
claims.quote: Dell HBA330 Mini firmware version 16.17.01.00 ... SAS Non-RAID ... PowerEdge R730 ... PowerEdge R730xd

claims.claim: In HBA mode a PERC 9 has no virtual disks and all disks run under OS control.
claims.quote: This mode does not contain virtual disks or the ability to create them. All physical disks function as non-RAID disks under operating system control.

claims.claim: PERC 9 controllers mostly ship in RAID mode.
claims.quote: RAID mode is commonly used and the controllers are mostly shipped from the factory in RAID mode.

claims.claim: TrueNAS says not to use a RAID card's RAID facility when it has an HBA mode.
claims.quote: do not use their RAID facility if your hardware RAID card supports HBA mode, also known as passthrough or JBOD mode

claims.claim: TrueNAS calls one RAID0 per disk not the ideal setup.
claims.quote: you can configure a RAID0 for every disk in your system. While not the ideal setup, it is functional when necessary.

claims.claim: TrueNAS lists masking of disk serial numbers and S.M.A.R.T. data among RAID card limitations.
claims.quote: can mask disk serial number and S.M.A.R.T. health information

claims.claim: The R730 supports two 300 W double-wide or four 150 W single-wide GPUs.
claims.quote: The R730 supports two 300W, full-length, double-wide GPUs or up to four 150W, full-length, single-wide GPUs.

claims.claim: Only passively cooled GPUs are supported.
claims.quote: Active cooled GPU cards not supported.

claims.claim: GPUs are for compute only, with no video out.
claims.quote: Note: GPU support is limited to compute and co-processing only; external video out is not supported.

claims.claim: GPUs sit on riser 2 and riser 3.
claims.quote: The GPUs are installed on the PCIe x16 3.0 interfaces available on riser 2 and GPU-optional riser 3.

claims.claim: Two double-wide GPUs need the optional single-x16 riser 3; three or four single-wide need the standard riser 3.
claims.quote: the optional riser 3 with a single x16 slot to support two double-wide GPUs. A standard riser 3 is required to support 3 or 4 single-wide GPUs.

claims.claim: Dell's GPU list includes NVIDIA K40, GRID K1 and K2 and AMD FirePro S7000 and S9050 (no K80).
claims.quote: NVIDIA K40 NVIDIA M20 NVIDIA K10 NVIDIA GRID™ K1 NVIDIA GRID K2 AMD S7000 FirePro AMD S9050 FirePro

claims.claim: Dell's GPU list includes Intel Xeon Phi coprocessors.
claims.quote: Intel Xeon Phi™ 5110P coprocessor Intel Xeon Phi 7120P coprocessor Intel Xeon Phi 3120P coprocessor

claims.claim: For the NVIDIA K80, Dell asks for two 1100 W supplies in non-redundant mode.
claims.quote: ensure that you install both PSUs with a minimum of 1100 W each and set the PSU configuration to non-redundant mode

claims.claim: StorageReview's R730 review describes the same GPU options.
claims.quote: up to four 150W single-width accelerators/GPUs or up to two 300W dual-width accelerators/GPUs

claims.claim: The R730xd does not support GPUs (quoted in What breaks).
claims.quote: The R730xd does not support internal or external GPUs.

claims.claim: Dell's comparison table lists internal GPUs as not supported on the R730xd.
claims.quote: 2 x 300W (double-wide) or 4 x 150W (single-wide) Not supported on R730xd

claims.claim: The GPU enablement kit carries the power cables and is described for the R730 chassis.
claims.quote: The kit contains the power cables and other items to enable GPU support on the R730 chassis.

claims.claim: Each GPU takes power through the enablement kit.
claims.quote: each GPU has up to two power connectors for power delivery. The GPU enablement kit is required for internal GPU installation.

claims.claim: The R730xd's slot 4 is a full-height x16 slot on processor 2.
claims.quote: 4 2 Processor 2 Full Height Full Length x16 x16

claims.claim: GPUs require redundant 1100 W power supplies.
claims.quote: your system uses the redundant 1100 W power supplies

claims.claim: GPUs require both processors installed.
claims.quote: both the processors are installed

claims.claim: GPU configurations need the kit's low-profile heat sinks.
claims.quote: The processor must use a GPU kit low-profile heat sink

claims.claim: With GPUs, inlet air is limited to 30C.
claims.quote: ambient inlet temperature is restricted to 30°C to ensure adequate cooling when one or more GPU cards are installed

claims.claim: The usual standard is 35C.
claims.quote: Note that this temperature is less than the standard environmental specification of 35oC.

claims.claim: Technical guide: GPU configurations need processors of 120 W or less.
claims.quote: Processors must be 120W or less

claims.claim: Owner's manual: GPU configurations need processors of 135 W or less.
claims.quote: The processor must be of 135 W or less

claims.claim: The 14-core E5-2695 v3 and E5-2683 v3 are 120 W parts in Dell's table.
Typical 3.5-inch R730: 28 dBA idle, 33 dBA operating.
claims.quote: Typically configured(2) 3.5” chassis in 23 ± 2 °C ambient ... Idle(3): LwA-UL(4) = 4.7 bels; LpA(5)= 28 dBA ... Operating(3): LwA-UL(4) = 5.3 bels; LpA(5)= 33 dBA

claims.claim: Typical 3.5-inch R730xd: 32 dBA idle, 43 dBA operating.
claims.quote: Idle(3): LwA-UL(4) = 5.1 bels; LpA(5)= 32 dBA; No prominent tones(6) ... Operating(3): LwA-UL(4) = 6.1 bels; LpA(5)= 43 dBA

claims.claim: Dell's typical 3.5-inch R730 has six drives.
claims.quote: For 3.5” chassis: 2 x 105W-10C CPU (Intel E5-2660 v3), 8 x 8GB DIMM, 6 x 3.5” SATA HDD

claims.claim: Dell's typical 3.5-inch R730xd has ten drives.
claims.quote: For 3.5” chassis: 2 x 85W-8C CPU (Intel E5-2630 v3), 8 x 8GB DIMM, 10 x 3.5” SATA HDD

claims.claim: A 3.5-inch R730xd with 16 drives is about 50% louder at idle than one with four (6.2 vs 5.6 bels).
claims.quote: configuration with 16 drives will be about 50% louder in idle condition than one with four drives (6.2 bels vs. 5.6 bels)

claims.claim: Any GPGPU card makes the R730 about twice as loud.
claims.quote: A configuration with any GPGPU card will be significantly louder (about twice as loud) than the typical configuration.

claims.claim: PCIe SSD configurations need more airflow and can reach 7.0 bels.
claims.quote: requires more airflow for cooling and will be significantly louder than a typical configuration. Under highly-stressed condition, the sound power levels may go up to 7.0 bels.

claims.claim: Low-power E5-2650L v3 and E5-2630L v3 configurations run about twice as loud under moderate or heavy load.
claims.quote: such as an Intel Xeon E5-2650L v3 or E52630L v3 at 65W CPU, under moderate or heavy utilization, will be about twice as loud as typical configurations.

claims.claim: Low-power CPUs have lower temperature limits.
claims.quote: (which have lower temperature limits than standard CPUs)

claims.claim: The default Power Optimized (DAPC) profile runs fans slower.
claims.quote: The system default setting is “Power Optimized (DAPC)”, which is in general a lower fan speed and noise level.

claims.claim: An owner reports about 17,000 RPM idle fans with a ConnectX-3 card and about 5,000 RPM without it.
claims.quote: Without any load, each of the 6 server fans runs at about 17000 RPM !! ... fans speed drops to ~5000 RPM

claims.claim: Both are 13th-generation servers with iDRAC8.
claims.quote: Dell's 13G servers come with version 8 of the iDRAC management platform.

claims.claim: iDRAC8 End of Sale December 2021; End of Software Maintenance February 2024.
claims.quote: iDRAC8 has reached the End of Sale as of December 2021 and reaches the End of Software Maintenance as of February 2024.

claims.claim: The last iDRAC8 firmware is 2.86.86.86.
claims.quote: The last release of iDRAC8 firmware is version 2.86.86.86.

claims.claim: Dell's definition of the End of Software Maintenance date.
claims.quote: The last date for Dell iDRAC Engineering to release any software maintenance releases or issue fixes.

claims.claim: A Dell moderator said no article lists PowerEdge end-of-life dates (reported as a forum exchange).
claims.quote: There isn't any article or documentation on PowerEdge EOL/EOSL/EOSS dates.

claims.claim: A Dell moderator told an owner the NVMe kit's extender goes in slot 4, which needs two processors, and that field backplane changes are not supported (reported as a forum exchange).
claims.quote: The expander should go in slot 4 ... you need two processors to use slot 4 ... field change to backplane configuration is not supported

claims.claim: The R730xd card table reserves slot 4 (priority 1, max 1) for a PCIe bridge card.
claims.quote: 1 PCIe Bridge 4 1
